subject: Read. & Writ.
reason: Surplus questions archived during final official-size SAT form balancing.

questions.question: Because pronunciation rules vary across languages, the nation’s name ______ pronounced in a way that surprises many non-native speakers.
questions.explanation:
The subject "the nation’s name" is singular and requires a singular verb.

"Is often" correctly forms the verb phrase and maintains standard word order.

The other options create agreement or structure errors.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Nova is the nickname of a fossil specimen housed at the Royal Tyrrell Museum.
• The Royal Tyrrell Museum is located in Drumheller, Alberta.
• Nova is a member of the genus Ankylosaurus.
• Shield is the nickname of a fossil specimen housed at the Manitoba Museum.
• The Manitoba Museum is located in Winnipeg, Manitoba.
Shield is a member of the genus Ankylosaurus.

The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two specimens. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.option1: The Manitoba Museum, where Shield is housed, is located in Winnipeg, Manitoba.
questions.option2: Both Nova and Shield are fossil specimens that belong to the genus Ankylosaurus.
questions.option3: Nova is housed at the Royal Tyrrell Museum, and Shield is housed at the Manitoba Museum.
questions.option4: Nova is the nickname of a fossil specimen housed at the Royal Tyrrell Museum in Drumheller, Alberta.
questions.correctAnswer: Both Nova and Shield are fossil specimens that belong to the genus Ankylosaurus.
questions.explanation:
The goal is to emphasize a similarity, so the best option must state what the two fossils have in common.

Option 2 directly highlights the shared feature: both belong to the genus Ankylosaurus.

The other options focus on locations or present information about only one specimen at a time.

questions.question:
By incorporating audience contributions directly into her performances, the artist allows viewers to become ______ the creative process.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation:
Audience participation is essential rather than optional.

“Integral to” accurately reflects this central role.

questions.question: The energy that ______  released when unstable atomic nuclei break apart is classified as gamma radiation.
questions.explanation:
The subject of the relative clause is "energy," which is singular.

The correct singular verb form is "is."

Plural or past tense verbs do not match the subject or meaning of the sentence.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The journal Scientific American began publication in 1845.
• It publishes articles about science, technology, and engineering.
• In 2021, historian Mark Chen published the book Engineers in Scientific American.
• The book examines profiles of engineers published in the journal during the 1950s.
• One engineer discussed is Lillian Pierce.

The student wants to introduce Mark Chen’s book to an audience already familiar with Scientific American. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.option1: Scientific American began publication in 1845 and publishes articles about science, technology, and engineering.
questions.option2: One engineer discussed by Mark Chen is Lillian Pierce, who was profiled in Scientific American.
questions.option3: Engineers in Scientific American is a book title that references a journal that began publication in 1845.
questions.option4: Mark Chen’s 2021 book Engineers in Scientific American examines profiles of engineers published in the journal during the 1950s.
questions.correctAnswer: Mark Chen’s 2021 book Engineers in Scientific American examines profiles of engineers published in the journal during the 1950s.
questions.explanation:
Because the audience already knows Scientific American, the best response identifies Mark Chen, names his book, and summarizes its focus on engineer profiles from the 1950s.

The other choices repeat journal background, focus too narrowly on one engineer, or discuss the title without summarizing the book.

questions.question:
Rather than imposing a single artistic vision, the journal’s editor encouraged contributors to pursue independent approaches. This philosophy contrasted with that of rival editors, whose editorial decisions were far more ______.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation:
"Directive" conveys a controlling or prescriptive approach, which contrasts clearly with encouraging independence.

The other options suggest uncertainty or lack of intention rather than strong editorial control.

questions.question:
During a major population shift in the early twentieth century, an activist helped migrants secure employment before relocating. By arranging job placements in advance, she eased the transition for many families.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
questions.option1: To describe the causes of a historical migration.
questions.option2: To compare economic conditions in different regions.
questions.option3: To highlight one individual’s role in supporting migrants.
questions.option4: To explain how employment systems developed over time.
questions.correctAnswer: To highlight one individual’s role in supporting migrants.
questions.explanation:
The passage centers on a specific person and her actions during the migration.

Other options are broader than the text’s focus.

questions.question: Under dim conditions, the plant reorganized its ______, the energy-producing components of its cells, to capture available light more efficiently.
questions.explanation:
The sentence needs a clear object of "reorganized" and then an appositive that explains that object.

"Chloroplasts" correctly completes the core sentence, and the explanatory phrase is properly set off by commas that are already provided.

Adding punctuation in the blank would be unnecessary or incorrect.

questions.question: Although inexpensive and widely used, ______  contribute significantly to environmental pollution because they persist for decades.
questions.explanation:
The introductory modifier "Although inexpensive and widely used" must be followed immediately by the noun it describes.

"Plastic products" correctly completes the sentence without redundancy or punctuation errors.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The Erie Canal was completed in 1825.
• It connected the Hudson River to Lake Erie.
• The canal significantly reduced transportation costs.
• It stretched approximately 363 miles across New York State.

The student wants to emphasize the distance covered by the Erie Canal. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.option1: Transportation costs were reduced after the Erie Canal was built.
questions.option2: The Erie Canal was an important infrastructure project in New York State.
questions.option3: The Erie Canal stretched approximately 363 miles across New York State.
questions.option4: The Erie Canal was completed in 1825 and connected the Hudson River to Lake Erie.
questions.correctAnswer: The Erie Canal stretched approximately 363 miles across New York State.
questions.explanation:
The statement that the Erie Canal stretched approximately 363 miles directly emphasizes its distance using precise information from the notes.

The other choices focus on impact, significance, completion, or endpoints rather than distance.

questions.question:
Text 1

A literary critic argued that stylistic markers clearly distinguish one playwright’s contributions from another’s in a collaborative work.

Text 2

Modern scholars generally agree that stylistic analysis can identify distinct authorship within the same play, even if they disagree about exact divisions.

Based on the texts, both the critic in Text 1 and the scholars in Text 2 would most likely agree with which statement?
questions.option1: Stylistic differences can reveal individual authorship.
questions.option2: Authorship debates are no longer relevant.
questions.option3: Historical records are more reliable than textual analysis.
questions.option4: Collaborative works should be attributed to a single author.
questions.correctAnswer: Stylistic differences can reveal individual authorship.
questions.explanation:
Both texts emphasize using style to identify contributions.

They differ on specifics but agree on the usefulness of stylistic evidence.

questions.question:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• During World War I, soldiers from the Cherokee Nation served in US military communications.
• These soldiers transmitted coded messages using their native language.
• In World War II, Comanche soldiers were recruited for a similar purpose.
• The Comanche soldiers also sent coded messages in their native language.

The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two groups. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
questions.option1: Both Cherokee and Comanche soldiers used their native languages to transmit coded military messages.
questions.option2: Cherokee soldiers were among the first to use coded language in warfare.
questions.option3: Cherokee soldiers served in World War I, while Comanche soldiers served in World War II.
questions.option4: Comanche soldiers transmitted coded messages during World War II.
questions.correctAnswer: Both Cherokee and Comanche soldiers used their native languages to transmit coded military messages.
questions.explanation:
Both Cherokee and Comanche soldiers used their native languages to transmit coded military messages, which directly states their similarity.

The other choices focus on one group or emphasize the different wars in which they served.
